options.tradeoff: Three explicit steps (choose, check, watch) cost one extra click versus a single form, and in exchange a bad file is visible before anything is written.

reference_evidence.application: The error report reuses the table density so row numbers and columns line up with the source file.
Import history is a server-paged table with the same footer, so a long history stays scannable.

reference_fidelity.copied: 44px header, full-opacity separators, hover on the row
reference_fidelity.deviated: The wizard itself is a two-column field grid, not a card stack
reference_fidelity.reason: Two fields (data type and file) do not earn a card each; a grid keeps them on one line at desktop width.

reference_fidelity.deviated: No per-column filter row; the toolbar holds one search box
reference_fidelity.reason: Import history is searched by data type label, not by five columns.

options.tradeoff: Rejected: one submit means the first feedback arrives after rows are already written, and the user cannot see which line failed until the batch finishes.

reference_evidence.application: Same table density, but with no report step to attach it to.
The history table keeps the footer even without a report step.

reference_fidelity.reason: A single request cannot report per-row progress, so the cancel and resume actions have nowhere to live.

notes: Import/export is an operational surface: the wizard's job is to make a bad file visible before it writes, so the dry-run report is the visual centerpiece, and the history table uses the shared ResourceTable frame with the export action in its header. Progress uses the shared Progress atom; status uses one badge with a single accent hue.
